label: Renting in England
headline: Black mould in your rented flat? Do this first
sub: 5 steps before you touch it, clean it or move out.

tips.title: Photograph it first
tips.text: Dated photos of every patch, with something for scale – plus a wide shot of the room.

tips.title: Gear up
tips.text: Goggles, long rubber gloves and a mask over your nose and mouth.

tips.title: Wipe gently – never brush
tips.text: Soapy water on small patches. Brushing can release spores.

tips.title: Report it in writing
tips.text: Tell your landlord or agent in writing and keep copies of every reply. Fixing the cause is usually their job.

tips.title: Still ignored? Call the council
tips.text: For serious problems you can ask for an environmental health inspection – the council can order a fix.

caption:

label: Renting in England
headline: Landlord put the rent up? Check these 5 things first
sub: The rules changed on 1 May 2026. General info, not legal advice.

tips.title: Once a year – never in year one
tips.text: No rise in your first year, and the next can't start until a year after the last one.

tips.title: It must be on form 4A
tips.text: Since 1 May 2026 a rise needs the official section 13 notice – form 4A.

tips.title: At least two months' notice
tips.text: Count from when you got the notice to the date the new rent starts.

tips.title: A text may not count
tips.text: Notices by email only count if your tenancy agreement says notices can be sent by email.

tips.title: You can challenge it
tips.text: Apply to the tribunal before the new rent starts – and keep paying your current rent meanwhile.

caption:
Landlord just told you the rent's going up? 😳 In England the rules changed on 1 May 2026 – and a lot of rent rises don't follow them.

Save this, and send it to the housemate who pays the landlord 👇

label: Renting in England
headline: Boiler broken and the landlord's dragging their feet? Do this
sub: England, private renters. General info, not legal advice.

tips.title: It's your landlord's job
tips.text: Keeping the boiler, radiators and hot water working is their legal repair – you can't sign it away.

tips.title: Report it, then put it in writing
tips.text: Ring or message straight away, then confirm by email so there's a dated record.

tips.title: Smell gas? 0800 111 999
tips.text: The gas emergency freephone. Open doors and windows and don't use anything you think is unsafe.

tips.title: Don't withhold rent
tips.text: Shelter warns arrears can lead to possession proceedings. Keep paying and get advice.

tips.title: Still not fixed? Call the council
tips.text: Ask for private sector housing or environmental health – they can act on serious hazards.

caption:
No heating, no hot water, and the landlord's "getting someone out"... again? 🥶

In England keeping the boiler working is your landlord's legal job. Report it, put it in writing, keep paying rent – and know when to call the council.

label: Christmas in a rented flat
headline: Decorate a rented flat for Christmas – without losing your deposit
sub: Hang, clip, lean or stand. Never stick or nail.

tips.title: Check your tenancy first
tips.text: Look for anything about adhesives or fixings – and photograph the walls before you start.

tips.title: Hang it, don't stick it
tips.text: Over-door hooks, curtain-pole clips and tension rods hold garlands and baubles with no fixings.

tips.title: Wrap and drape fairy lights
tips.text: Round a banister, curtain pole or headboard – or battery lights in a jar on the windowsill.

tips.title: Go small with the tree
tips.text: A tabletop or slim pencil tree, on a mat, away from radiators and heaters.

tips.title: Wreath without a nail
tips.text: An over-door wreath hanger hooks over the top of the door. Nothing to screw in.

caption:
Want your rented flat to feel like Christmas without a single nail hole? 🎄

The rule: hang, clip, lean or stand – never stick. Doors, curtain poles and banisters are your best friends this December.
